data.title: What is ChatGPT Wallet, how does it work and who can use it?
data.description:
OpenAI has given its AI agents a way to pay. ChatGPT Wallet, unveiled on Friday, lets the company’s “dots” agents complete purchases for users, provided the user signs off on each one.

OpenAI set out the details in a blog post and a help-centre guide.

Built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, the feature starts small, but it is OpenAI’s second attempt in just over a year to take ChatGPT from product research to the checkout.

What is ChatGPT Wallet?

ChatGPT Wallet is a payment feature inside dots, the always-on personal agents OpenAI unveiled at its DevDay conference on 29 September.

Until now, a dot that found a sweater or a hotel room still needed a human to finish checkout. With Wallet, users save a card once, and the agent pays through the merchant’s normal checkout.

Cards saved in Wallet are kept separate from the one that pays for the ChatGPT subscription, and from any prepaid ChatGPT balance.

How does ChatGPT Wallet work?

OpenAI’s guidance describes five stages. The user adds a card through a secure form rather than in the chat, and the bank may ask for verification. The user then asks their dot to find something, such as a hotel for a weekend trip.

Before paying, the dot shows the merchant, items, total, chosen card and any recurring-payment terms. The user approves with a biometric check such as Face ID or Touch ID, creating a record of what was authorised.

Finally, the card network issues a payment token, a substitute card number, security code and expiry date, which the agent enters at checkout. The real card details are never shared with the agent or the merchant, OpenAI says.

OpenAI is not taking a fee on transactions at launch, according to CNBC. The sale is between shopper and merchant, which keeps control of pricing, delivery and returns.

Who can use ChatGPT Wallet?

Wallet is open only to ChatGPT Pro subscribers, whose plans cost $100 to $500 a month. Users must be 18 or over, live in the US and hold an eligible US-issued card with a US billing address. It works only in conversations with a dot.

OpenAI’s help centre lists eligible Chase cards for primary cardholders, alongside Amex, Mastercard and Visa. Virtual cards are not supported at launch.

There is no timetable for Free, Go or Plus users, or for the UK and Europe. Amex’s Luke Gebb told CNBC the narrow rollout was deliberate.

What does it mean for consumers?

The main gain is convenience: an agent can take a purchase from search to payment without the user retyping card details.

OpenAI says shoppers keep their card rewards and protections for eligible disputes, such as a faulty item. Refunds go through the merchant, and unrecognised charges through the card issuer.

There are drawbacks. OpenAI concedes some sites may block agents or flag their purchases as fraud. Amazon stops agents buying on its platform, CNBC reported, and United Airlines said this week it would block third-party AI agents from booking. OpenAI also tells users that a “ready to check out” message does not confirm an order.

Privacy is another consideration. Merchants may still need a name, phone number, email and delivery address, which can be passed on through the conversation.

Longer term, OpenAI wants users to pre-approve purchases within spending limits, categories or time windows, so the agent need not ask each time. It has given no date for that.

Why is OpenAI doing this?

OpenAI says 1.2 billion people use ChatGPT each week, many of them to research what to buy, and it had nearly 100 million paying users at the end of the third quarter, CNBC reported.

Its first checkout push stalled. Instant Checkout, launched in September 2025 with the Agentic Commerce Protocol built alongside Stripe, was wound down in March, when OpenAI said it lacked flexibility for merchants.

Wallet takes a different route, using merchants’ existing checkouts and the card networks’ token systems. OpenAI is also working with payment firms including Stripe and Adyen, and fraud-prevention specialists such as Forter and Signifyd, so genuine agent purchases are not wrongly declined.

How have markets reacted?

OpenAI is privately held, so attention turned to its listed partners.

At 16:55 GMT, Visa was up 1.4% at $426.20 and Mastercard 1.4% at $661.46 against Thursday’s close, while Amex was 0.5% higher at $319.77, according to Yahoo Finance data.

The moves are modest and cannot be pinned on the launch alone.

What happens next?

OpenAI has published a Commerce Partner Playbook showing merchants how to let its agents through and share product feeds. It says it will widen access once it has learned from early use with businesses, banks and card networks.

data.title: Kraken owner Payward’s Q3 adjusted EBITDA falls 67% as trading volumes slide
data.description:
Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, reported a sharp fall in third-quarter profit from a year earlier, even as results recovered from a weak second quarter.

In its Q3 2026 financial highlights, published on Friday, November 13, the company said adjusted EBITDA was $60 million, up from $23 million in the second quarter. Bloomberg, which reviewed Payward’s shareholder letter, reported that the figure was down 67% year on year.

Payward also changed how it reports. It now uses Total Platform Margin (TPM) in place of adjusted revenue, deducting both the cost of crypto delivered to clients and the staking rewards it pays out. On that basis TPM was $487 million, up 12% from $436 million in Q2 and down 12% from a year earlier.

Volumes down on the year, up on the quarter

Total platform transaction volume was $353 billion, which Payward said was 22% higher than in Q2 but 30% lower than in Q3 2025.

The company said it grew while industry spot volume fell 7% quarter on quarter, citing CoinMarketCap data, and that its share of industry spot volume rose to 6.5% in September from 3.3% a year earlier.

Bloomberg linked the annual decline to softer crypto prices. Bitcoin rallied roughly 40% from mid-August to early October before retreating on inflation worries and concern over how the US midterm elections could affect the industry. Exchanges that depend on trading fees tend to see activity slow when prices fall.

Average assets on platform were $43 billion, down 21% year on year. Payward said that at constant prices they rose 29% to $71 billion, and that clients had added assets in each of the last 12 months.

Less reliance on trading fees

The company is trying to show that its business is no longer just about spot trading. It split TPM into three buckets for the first time:

  • transaction-based TPM rose 7% quarter on quarter to $234 million;
  • asset-based TPM, earned on assets clients hold, rose 26% to $128 million;
  • access-based TPM, from subscriptions, trader evaluations, listings and index licences, rose 7% to $125 million.

Asset- and access-based income together made up 52% of the total, up from 46% a year earlier. Derivatives contracts traded rose 84% year on year to 66 million, billable accounts rose 74% to 1.5 million, and funded accounts rose 37% to 7.1 million. Payward notes that funded accounts are not a count of unique clients, as one client can hold several.

Tokenised stocks, banking and AI agents

Payward said its xStocks tokenised equities business passed $1 billion in assets under management in October and now offers more than 700 tokenised stocks. Earlier this week it added hundreds of UK and EU-listed shares, including the DAX 40.

In the US it plans to offer onchain perpetual futures, starting on Hyperliquid, and single-stock perpetual futures, both subject to regulatory approval. Prediction markets for US clients are listed as a next step, though the company gave no timing. In October it agreed to buy Saldo Bank, an EU-licensed digital bank, with completion subject to regulatory approval.

Payward also named AI as a fifth business pillar alongside trading, banking, asset management and Payward Services. It said every Payward app will get an “agent harness” through which clients can direct AI agents across their holdings, with the first expected early next year. It also plans to launch a personal finance agent, designed to act only within client-set limits and with client approval before a trade runs.

On regulation, Payward said Kraken plans to launch in the UAE following full market approval from Dubai’s Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA), and that it has received in-principle approval from Kazakhstan’s AFSA.

Bloomberg has previously reported that Payward’s initial public offering may not happen until next year.

For more on the exchange’s fees, products and licences, see our Kraken review. Readers comparing platforms can also check our guide to the best crypto exchanges.

data.title: It's not just Nvidia, IonQ stock is also slipping on leadership shake-up
data.description:
Nvidia isn’t the only technology company facing investor scrutiny over a leadership change.

IonQ (IONQ) stock tanked on November 13 after the quantum computing company announced an immediate executive departure and a reshuffle of its finance team.

The disclosure brings uncertainty just over a week after IONQ raised its revenue outlook – leaving investors weighing fast commercial expansion against management shake-up and the considerable cost of building the business.

Why finance team reshuffle is hurting IonQ stock

In its press release, IonQ said CFO Inder Singh is stepping down immediately, and Gary Merril – the current chief of finance at Commvault – will replace him in early December.

The company also appointed former Juniper Networks’ senior executive Thomas Austin to a newly created chief accounting officer position.

The bearish implication is uncertainty over financial leadership during an expansion that requires careful spending and acquisition integration.

An abrupt transition can make investors demand stronger evidence that execution remains on track.

However, the appointments alone provide no basis for concluding that IonQ Inc faces accounting problems.

Experienced replacements may ultimately strengthen oversight as the business grows.

In short, the sell-off in IONQ stock today reflects uncertainty; where that uncertainty becomes a lasting concern depends on what the incoming team delivers.

Is it worth buying the dip in IONQ shares today?

IonQ shares retain a credible growth case.

The company reported Q3 sales of nearly $174 million, up a whopping 336% year-on-year, and raised its 2026 guidance to $505 million at least.

That said, investors must examine the composition: acquired foundry SkyWater contributed $83.5 million, nearly half the quarterly sales total.

IonQ’s platform segment separately grew a whopping 127% to $90.3 million.

That distinction matters when valuing the stock.

Buying a larger revenue base does not establish how quickly existing operations can expand – or how profitable the combined company will become.

The latest quarter also included a $133.6 million adjusted EBITDA loss.

So IonQ Inc may interest investors comfortable with substantial execution risk, but a lower share price alone doesn’t establish a bargain.

What investors should watch before calling a bottom

IonQ has financial resources to support its ambitions.

It reported $1.7 billion in cash, equivalents and investments at September 30, rising to $3.7 billion on a pro forma basis after October’s $2 billion equity offering.

That financing provides flexibility, although issuing shares dilutes existing ownership.

For prospective buyers, the more useful signals are continued platform growth, progress toward lower operating losses and disciplined integration of acquired businesses.

Clear communication from the incoming finance team would also help investors assess spending priorities.

What’s also worth mentioning is that today’s decline in IONQ shares coincides with weakness in quantum computing stocks at large, so the leadership announcement doesn’t explain every percentage point lost.

IonQ’s challenge is to demonstrate that its expanding business can create durable shareholder value alongside impressive revenue growth.

data.title: These 3 stocks stand to benefit from the Jensen Huang saga
data.description:
Nvidia’s (NVDA) leadership crisis is giving investors a reason to look beyond the AI chips darling.

The company’s share price came under pressure this week as Jensen Huang resigned, and the board named CFO Colette Kress as the interim chief executive of NVDA.

The upheaval could encourage customers to diversify their suppliers, creating major opportunities for competitors.

Three stocks stand out: Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom and Alphabet. Each offers a different route into the AI spending boom – and a potential way to capitalize on the recent Nvidia fallout.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)

AMD has the clearest opening if Nvidia’s customers accelerate efforts to find another supplier of AI chips.

Bloomberg Intelligence’s senior expert Mandeep Singh expects NVDA to be more cautious under its new chief, creating room for rivals to capture market share.

For AMD stock, the opportunity is to turn customers’ concerns about supplier concentration into a stronger position in future purchasing decisions.

It closed higher on Thursday – reflecting investor enthusiasm for that possibility.

That said, interest must translate into orders before the financial benefits become clear.

Switching AI workloads takes time and money, making upcoming contracts and deployments more meaningful evidence of progress than the stock’s immediate reaction to Huang’s departure.

Wall Street currently has a consensus Buy rating on AMD shares.

Broadcom (AVGO)

Broadcom could benefit as Nvidia’s turmoil strengthens the argument for custom AI chips.

Its pivotal role in developing specialized processors and networking equipment gives it exposure to customers seeking greater control over their computing infrastructure.

AVGO shares are another potential beneficiary if Nvidia’s leadership fiasco disrupts customer relationships. That was substantiated by a notable rally in Broadcom on Nov. 12.

Note that the company has already been seeing massive demand for custom AI chips, helping fiscal Q3 soar 86% on a year-over-year basis to $29.6 billion.

A 0.74% dividend yield makes Broadcom even more attractive for long-term investors.

Wall Street currently rates AVGO at Buy.

Alphabet (GOOGL)

Alphabet also offers an alternative through its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) – giving AI clients another option as they reconsider their dependence on Nvidia.

Broader TPU adoption could strengthen Google Cloud by attracting businesses seeking different infrastructure for training and running AI models.

Bloomberg Intelligence expects TPU sales to exceed $50 billion next year, highlighting the potential scale of that opportunity.

Google shares closed nearly 2% higher on Thursday.

Its challenge is converting renewed customer interest into sustained usage: TPUs cannot replace GPUs across every application, and migration can be costly.

Even so, Nvidia’s leadership uncertainty could give Google another reason to enter purchasing discussions, potentially accelerating adoption of an alternative it was already expanding.

Wall Street currently has a consensus Buy rating on GOOGL shares.

data.title: Trump Media stock jumped after earnings: beware of key risks
data.description:
Trump Media stock bounced back this week after the company announced its financial results, which showed strong revenue and profitability growth. DJT jumped to $5, up by over 40% from its lowest point this month. Still, the company faces some major risks as Bitcoin falls and as Democrats prepares to take power.

Trump Media stock jumps after earnings

Trump Media, the parent company of Truth Social, published its third-quarter report, which provided insights about its business. The results showed that the company’s revenue jumped by 205% in the third quarter to $3 million. This revenue was driven by Truth API, the newly launched service that gives users the ability to pay for early access of Trump’s social media posts.

Most notably, the company said that its profit jumped during the quarter. It jumped to $409.7 million in the third quarter, much higher than the losses it generated in the same period last year. 

However, the reality is that these growth catalysts face some major risks ahead. First, Democrats won the midterm elections by a large margin. They are on track to win 56 seats in the Senate and more than 250 in the House of Representatives. Since corruption was one of the biggest issues in this election, Democrats will likely probe Trump Media for the Truth API solution.

Critics argue that the company is engaging in illegalities by allowing Trump to benefit from his social media posts. In other words, he is allowing rich high-frequency trading companies to have market-moving information before the rest of the market.

The other crucial risk that Trump Media faces is the ongoing Bitcoin price weakness. Bitcoin plunged to $67,700, down by over 22% from its highest point in September this year. It has moved to its lowest level since August 20th this year. 

The ongoing Bitcoin weakness is important for Trump Media because it is one of the biggest holders. It holds 15,649 coins, making it the 9th-largest Bitcoin holder in the world. Its Bitcoin holdings explain why its profit jumped in the third quarter as the coin jumped from $57,700 to $126,300 in October.

Further, the decision to merge with TAE Technologies faces risks since the company is not yet profitable. It was established in 1998 and has spent this period researching on its technology. While it has made substantial progress in this period, it is still unclear whether it will become a profitable company in the long term. 

Meanwhile, data compiled by SimilarWeb shows that Truth Social is not a popular social media platform. Its website visitors dropped by 22% in October from September. It has dropped by over 50% from a year earlier, a trend that has accelerated as Trump’s approval rating plunged. This trend will continue after the last midterm election in which the Republican party lost big.

DJT stock price technical analysis

Trump Media stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the Trump Media stock has been in a strong freefall this year and is now hovering near its all-time low. It has remained below the important support level of $6.85, its lowest level on June 26. 

The stock has remained below the 50-day and 100-day moving averages and the Supertrend indicators. Also, there is a risk that the ongoing rebound is a dead-cat bounce, a temporary rebound that is often followed by a retreat.

Therefore, the stock will likely resume the downward trend, and retest the support level of $3.7, its lowest level this week. A move below that level will point to more downside, potentially to the psychological level of $3.0.

data.title: Why SpaceX shares are sliding ahead of historic Starship Flight 15 launch?
data.description:
SpaceX SPCX shares fell on Friday ahead of a high-stakes Starship test flight, with investors also weighing growing scrutiny of Elon Musk's potential merger plans involving Tesla.

The stock traded 1% lower on Friday at around 11:45 AM EDT.

Major US indexes also moved lower, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq shedding over 1.6% as investors continued to digest headlines around outgoing Nvidia chief Jensen Huang

Tesla merger faces growing political scrutiny

One factor weighing on SpaceX was increased scrutiny of its potential merger with Tesla.

Bloomberg reported on Thursday that the companies could announce a deal as soon as December.

However, the changing political environment could bring greater scrutiny to merger discussions involving two of the state's most valuable companies.

At the federal level, Democrats who took control of Congress have signaled plans to investigate Musk's business and political activities.

Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson has vowed to take a close look at the potential merger.

"Any merger of companies of that consequence warrants tremendous scrutiny," Johnson told Bloomberg.

He also raised concerns about the concentration of private and public-sector influence around Musk.

"I don't want anybody to have such control of the public sector that they can bend public power to their private gain. I think his Empire is at great risk of crossing that line," Johnson said of Musk.

However, Johnson also indicated a willingness to have discussions with the world's richest man, who donated heavily, but in vain, to Republican causes during the midterm elections.

Analysts have also highlighted structural obstacles to combining the two companies, particularly the challenge of separating Tesla's substantial Chinese manufacturing operations from SpaceX's sensitive US defense contracts.

SpaceX restructures Grok Imagine team

Separately, SpaceX's AI division laid off roughly 60 employees from the Grok Imagine video-generation team, The Information reported on Friday.

The cuts leave only a small number of employees to maintain the image and video features of the Grok chatbot.

They form part of a restructuring following the earlier integration of xAI into SpaceX.

The move reflects a shift in resources toward coding tools and other priorities, while adding to questions about the future development of Grok's image and video-generation capabilities.

Starship Flight 15 becomes another major catalyst

Investors are also focused on Starship Flight 15, which is set to take place later on Friday.

The mission aims to achieve a historic recovery of both the Super Heavy booster and the upper-stage Starship using the launch tower's mechanical arms.

A successful recovery would mark an important advance in SpaceX's efforts to develop a rapidly reusable launch system.

It could also support denser Starlink deployments and the company's longer-term ambitions involving orbital computing infrastructure.

KeyBanc on Friday reiterated its Sector Weight rating on SpaceX, while expressing optimism about the upcoming Starship launch.

"The launch is a key milestone for the program, as SPCX seeks to demonstrate fixes and enhancements implemented following some anomalies encountered during Flight 14 in September 2026," the brokerage said.

Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas also reiterated an Overweight rating on SpaceX, maintaining his $300 price target.

Jonas described a successful catch of the Starship and Super Heavy booster as "one of the most significant potential catalysts in SpaceX's nearly 25-year history."

The upcoming flight therefore represents an important milestone for the company as it works to demonstrate the improvements made following Flight 14 and advance its reusable rocket program.

data.title: Cisco earnings were strong: why is the stock sliding then?
data.description:
Cisco Systems (CSCO) posted the kind of earnings report that usually sends investors reaching for the buy button.

Revenue came in at $18.5 billion, and earnings soared to $1.4 per share – up more than expected, 24% and 40% versus the same quarter last year.

Yet, Cisco stock opened in the red this morning.

The disconnect reflects a tougher question facing the networking giant: how much should investors pay for its AI expansion when margins are shrinking and order growth is losing speed?

Cisco stock sinks on a profitability trade-off

The first concern sits between Cisco’s sales and its bottom line. Adjusted gross margin dropped to 65.6% from 68.1% a year earlier.

Management attributed the squeeze to hardware growing faster than software and services, alongside elevated memory costs.

That matters because selling more equipment can produce impressive revenue growth while leaving CSCO with less gross profit from each sales dollar.

However, describing this as an earnings-quality collapse would go too far. Adjusted operating expenses increased just 2%, helping Cisco achieve a record 37.8% adjusted operating margin.

CSCO shares are under pressure primarily because of the durability concern.

Cost discipline is cushioning the changing sales mix today.

Sustaining that protection becomes harder if hiring, investment, or other expenses eventually accelerate.

Shareholders therefore need to watch both margins, rather than treating either one as the complete profitability story.

Strong orders leave investors questioning the pace

The second sticking point is the direction of demand.

Product orders increased 21% from a year earlier, a healthy result but slower than the preceding quarter’s 35% growth.

That made several Wall Street analysts reduce their price targets on Cisco shares after earnings, highlighting potential growth deceleration and tougher comparisons in campus networking.

Orders matter because they help investors assess future business, while reported revenue largely describes equipment and services already delivered.

A slowdown in bookings growth can therefore overshadow an acceleration in current sales.

Still, slower growth does not mean shrinking demand.

Cisco’s earnings call showed enterprise orders rising 15% and public-sector orders increasing 13%, suggesting spending strength extends beyond the biggest cloud operators.

The unresolved issue is whether those customers can sustain momentum as comparisons become more demanding.

Should you buy the dip in CSCO stock?

Cisco’s revised outlook gives investors a substantial counterargument to the selling.

Management now projects fiscal 2027 revenue of $74.8 billion at least and adjusted earnings of $5.47 to $5.53 per share.

It also expects $9 billion in AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers, more than twice the previous fiscal year’s total.

The forecast supports a growing business, but they do not automatically establish that CSCO stock is cheap.

The stronger investment case would combine continued order expansion with evidence that the hardware-heavy sales mix can support lasting profit growth.

Friday’s reaction suggests investors want that evidence before rewarding Cisco with a higher valuation.

data.title: US wholesale inflation rises less than expected in October
data.description:
US wholesale prices increased less than expected in October, offering some relief on the inflation front, although a sharp acceleration in annual producer prices and persistent cost pressures could complicate the Federal Reserve's next interest rate decision.

The producer price index (PPI), which measures the prices domestic producers receive for goods and services before they reach consumers, rose a seasonally adjusted 0.3% during the month, below the 0.4% increase expected by economists surveyed by Dow Jones, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Friday.

Core PPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, also increased 0.3%, in line with expectations.

However, the annual headline PPI rate accelerated to 6.5%, up 0.2 percentage points from the previous reading and marking its highest level since November 2022.

Goods prices drive annual producer inflation higher

The details of the report showed that inflationary pressures remained broad across several parts of the economy.

Prices for final demand goods increased 0.5% in October, although more than 60% of the advance came from goods excluding food and energy.

Prices in the latter category actually declined 0.1% during the month.

On an annual basis, the goods index jumped 10.2%, marking its biggest 12-month increase since October 2022.

Final demand services prices rose 0.2%, with much of the increase linked to transportation and warehousing services.

Truck transportation of freight recorded a 3.9% increase.

Meanwhile, prices for intermediate processed goods surged 14.6% from October 2025, the largest annual increase since July 2022.

Intermediate services prices climbed 6.9%, their biggest gain since November 2022.

A measure of producer prices that excludes food, energy and trade services increased 0.5% during October, pointing to continued cost pressures beyond volatile commodity markets.

Persistent inflation complicates Fed's December decision

The report comes ahead of the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting on December 8-9, with policymakers facing mounting questions over how to balance inflation risks against the broader economic outlook.

Earlier this week, the BLS reported that consumer inflation was hotter than expected in October.

Headline and core consumer prices both increased 0.4% and 0.3%, respectively, exceeding forecasts by 0.1 percentage point.

The latest readings suggest that inflation remains some distance from the Fed's 2% target.

Markets have been pricing in a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December 9 meeting as almost certain, with traders assigning a 100% probability to an increase, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.

The odds of a 25-basis-point hike stand at 89.7%, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point increase is 10.3%.

Policymakers are also concerned that higher fuel prices linked to the Iran war and President Donald Trump's tariffs could be spreading through the economy.

While the Fed might ordinarily look through temporary supply-driven price increases, their broadening impact could indicate that inflation is becoming more entrenched.

Stock futures extended their gains following the PPI release, while Treasury yields were mixed as investors assessed the implications for monetary policy.

data.title: Nvidia shares edge up on Friday: is the worst over?
data.description:
Nvidia NVDA shares edged higher in premarket trading on Friday, recovering slightly after a sharp selloff tied to the abrupt resignation of longtime CEO Jensen Huang.

The stock was up 2% ahead of the opening bell after closing Thursday at $166.19, down 4.3%.

That followed deeper losses earlier in the week as the leadership crisis intensified.

Trading has been volatile, with the stock hitting lows near $149 in the previous session before recovering.

Investors have been rattled by uncertainty over succession and the broader implications for Nvidia's dominant position in artificial intelligence chips.

Colette Kress, the company's former finance chief, has taken over as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement.

The premarket bounce suggests some dip-buying after the heavy selling, although shares remain well below recent highs.

The broader market was also in green in futures trading, with technology stocks continuing to reflect caution around the AI sector.

Opinions divided over Nvidia's short-term recovery

Wall Street analysts have responded with caution, with several warning that the leadership turmoil could weigh on the stock even as Nvidia's underlying business remains strong.

"Nvida's competitive advantage and customers don't disappear overnight," Seth Hickle, chief investment officer at Mindset Wealth Management, told Reuters.

"The market is trying to determine whether this is a temporary leadership crisis or something that fundamentally changes the AI investment thesis."

Hickle said implied volatility would likely remain elevated until Nvidia's earnings report and subsequent conference call provide more clarity about the company's plans following the leadership change.

Lior Prosor, managing partner at deep-tech venture capital and private equity fund Deep33, also expects continued uncertainty in the near term.

"In the short term, we expect the market to remain jittery. Investors will want clarity on permanent leadership and several quarters of evidence that NVIDIA continues to execute against its roadmap and delivery expectations," Prosor told Yahoo Finance.

"Until then, even if the stock looks increasingly cheap on fundamentals, it may take time before buying that discount becomes an easy trade."

Ryan Zurrer, founder and director of investment firm Dialectic, sees the selloff differently and considers the lower valuation an opportunity.

"You're buying this thing at 10 times forward-looking earnings for a company that, for all intents and purposes, seems irreplicable in the global AI infrastructure base," Zurrer was quoted as saying by Yahoo Finance.

Analysts downgrade Nvidia

Several analysts have either downgraded Nvidia shares or reduced their price targets following the latest developments.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon cut his price target from $400 and downgraded the stock from Market Outperform.

However, he maintained that the company's underlying business remained strong despite the leadership turmoil.

"Fundamentals of the business (if not the leadership) are clearly still intact with numbers that remain massive (and probably still headed higher). We don’t think the company should have huge issues operating while engaged in a search for new leadership. And (of course) the shares are almost absurdly cheap (and getting cheaper as we speak); clearly there is a lot of bad news getting priced in here," he said.

He nevertheless cautioned against making a large investment in the stock at this stage.

"On the other hand, we find it hard to advocate stepping in here in size as there will no doubt be more allegations to come," he said.

William Blair's Sebastien Naji downgraded Nvidia to Market Perform from Outperform, citing concerns about the potential impact of the controversy on the company's shares.

Naji believes the developments could remain a significant overhang on Nvidia stock in the near term.

"Meanwhile, the potential for a slower AI buildout and more intense competition from other chipmakers will only add to execution risk…governance and regulatory pressure, the potential for more serious fallout, and a sudden change in management are likely to muddle both execution and sentiment," he said.

Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer also downgraded Nvidia to Perform from Outperform.

"While we see upside to the F3Q (Oct.) print and F4Q (Jan.) outlook, we expect fundamentals to take a backseat near term. The departure of Mr. Huang could, in our view, translate to a lingering share overhang,” Schafer said.

Despite the downgrades and price target reductions, analysts continue to highlight Nvidia's strong AI product pipeline and long-term demand as supporting factors, even as they flag near-term governance and succession concerns.

Allegations keep coming

Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom US authorities have suspected of links to Chinese intelligence, was reported to have connections with China's Huawei, which has been blacklisted due to security concerns.

Jensen Huang was reportedly involved in a romantic relationship with the suspected Chinese agent.

Additional reports have emerged of a second relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reported to Huang.

On Thursday, Reuters reported that Huang had an intimate relationship with yet another Nvidia employee, citing people familiar with the situation.

Huang will be testifying before Congress ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

Nvidia is scheduled to report fiscal third-quarter earnings on 17 November, having previously forecast revenue of approximately $108 billion.

data.title: Palo Alto Networks stock rises as KeyBanc upgrades shares to Overweight
data.description:
Palo Alto Networks shares surged 3% in premarket trading on Friday after KeyBanc Capital Markets upgraded the cybersecurity company, citing expectations of stronger security spending and its position in the market for artificial intelligence protection.

KeyBanc raised its rating on Palo Alto Networks (PANW) to Overweight from Sector Weight and assigned a price target of $380.

The upgrade comes ahead of the company's fiscal first-quarter earnings report, scheduled for November 18.

The new target implies approximately 18% upside potential from Thursday's closing price.

The upgrade follows a roughly 20% decline in Palo Alto Networks shares over the past month.

KeyBanc said the pullback, alongside positive checks on the company's first-quarter performance, had created an attractive entry point.

KeyBanc sees stronger cybersecurity spending through 2027

KeyBanc analyst Eric Heath said the firm expects security budgets to accelerate through 2027, which could benefit Palo Alto Networks.

In a note to clients, Heath said the company was well positioned to benefit from the trend towards consolidation in cybersecurity, supported by its product offerings in areas including AI security.

He also pointed to the growing need for businesses to defend against threats associated with the accelerating adoption of artificial intelligence.

Heath said Palo Alto Networks was executing better than many of its cybersecurity peers, adding that the firm's positive first-quarter checks supported the decision to upgrade the stock.

The analyst also highlighted the recent share-price decline as a factor behind the improved investment opportunity.

Investors await Palo Alto Networks' quarterly results

Investors will now focus on Palo Alto Networks' fiscal first-quarter results, due on November 18, for further indications of demand across its cybersecurity business.

Analysts expect the company to report earnings of $0.97 per share on revenue of $3.31 billion, according to consensus estimates cited by Seeking Alpha.

The results could provide further insight into the company's ability to benefit from increased security spending and demand for solutions that protect businesses as they adopt AI technologies.

Palo Alto Networks provides network, cloud, and security operations solutions.

The company serves more than 80,000 enterprise customers worldwide, including over 75% of the Global 2000.

Its position across several areas of cybersecurity has also attracted attention from market commentators.

CNBC's Jim Cramer recently expressed confidence in Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike Holdings, saying he preferred the two companies over Netskope, another cloud security platform.

Cybersecurity stocks remain in focus

The KeyBanc upgrade comes as investors assess which cybersecurity companies are best positioned to benefit from changing enterprise security requirements.

The increasing use of AI creates opportunities for security providers, while also introducing new threats that businesses need to address.

KeyBanc's outlook rests partly on the expectation that companies will increase their security budgets through 2027 and that Palo Alto Networks will continue to execute ahead of many of its peers.

However, investors will be looking for confirmation of these trends in the company's upcoming results.

The November 18 earnings report will therefore be an important near-term event for the stock, as investors assess revenue performance, earnings, and management's outlook against expectations for stronger cybersecurity spending.
